sentences.text: Welcome everyone to Travel Report.
This is Scott Lam bringing you this week's edition.
Let's welcome our guests for this week’s podcast first of all.
I'm very pleased to have here in the pod tonight Adrian Lim.
Good evening. Adrian, you're a travel agent specialising in unusual holidays, is that right?
Yes, that’s right.
OK, and we also have with us, Dr.
Kelly Johnson.
Now, Kelly. You’ve been on the program lots of times before, but just for those who don’t know, you're a lecturer in travel and tourism.
Yeah, that’s right.
OK, let’s begin this week then, with the question, why do people travel?
Adrienne. Well, I suppose people go on holiday and travel for many different reasons Such as?
Well, a recent survey showed that the most popular reasons people gave for going on holiday and travelling are wanting to challenge themselves and have fun.
Yeah, that’s what I would have guessed people would say.
Sometimes we forget that having fun is as important as anything else.
Yeah, but people gave other reasons in their survey.
They want to do other things that’s why they travel like, say, learn a language.
That's another reason to travel Like me I guess.
I went to Japan after university to learn more Japanese.
Oh, So did I.
I’m not sure how much Japanese I learnt though.
Right so that’s a few reasons anyway.
we travel to challenge ourselves, have fun or learn a language.
So I suppose the reasons why people travel haven't changed much, but other aspects of travel may be half.
That's right. So what was different about travel international travel I mean in the past then?
Say in the 1920s?
Kelly? Well, the main differences about present day travel compared to the 1920s, I suppose, if we're talking about international travel are things things like the transport how people travelled
and the length of time.
I mean how long it took What was the transport?
By ship or train or?
Yeah, international travel meant people travelled by ship or by train Yeah, I was reading about this.
It took a long time, so that’s why holidays were longer.
longer. Like, it could take 6 weeks to travel by ship from London to Hong Kong for tourists!
Six weeks! Wow!
Can you imagine!
Now, nowadays it’s really common for lots of people from all countries to go abroad on holiday.
Was this always the case or is this a recent phenomenon?
I mean, was international travel an unusual holiday in itself in the past?
Well, from my own research into this, yes, you're right.
It was only the very rich people travel was very expensive and, well, with the transport and time, only rich people could do it So all of this holidays abroad is a new thing then?
Well, yes, it’s really been in the last 30 years that it’s really taken off.
So what's the most popular places to visit nowadays?
Maybe Adrian, you'd be the person to ask.
Right, I've got some statistics here.
Let me see.
Last year the most popular place to visit was India.
76 million people went there.
That’s certainly different from 20 years ago.
India. OK. Which other countries are popular?
Well, the USA has lots of visitors 59 million went there last year Wow!
59 million? That's a lot.
Yes, that’s only slightly more than China there were 55 million visitors.
55 million. I read or maybe someone told me that Spain is popular too.
Is that right?
Yeah, Spain’s still really popular it had about 52 million visitors last year, I think Well, I suppose all that tells us that more and more people are travelling.
But I suppose the next thing is what are they doing when they travel?
Well, one thing I’ve noticed is that our customers want to stay in different places like these new types of unusual hotels.
Oh, that’s interesting.
Can you give us an example of one of these unusual hotels?
Mm -hmm. Well, the ice hotels.
They’re popular. Ice hotels I’ve heard of them!
Is that like a hotel made of ice?
Exactly! Everything is made of ice the rooms, the beds, tables, chairs, everything!
Our customers really love them I’ve always wondered Are they cold?
No they aren’t cold.
But they are in cold countries!
I think I'd like to try staying in one!
Any more your unusual hotels Oh I know, there’s a prison hotel in Australia.
I stayed in it last year A prison hotel?
I thought you only stayed in a prison if you'd done something wrong!
Well, it’s not any old prison.
prison. In Australia, some old prisons have closed and then they have turned them into hotels.
Really? Yeah You can sleep in a cell like a prisoner but What in a cell?
You mean the hotel guests are locked up for the night in a prison cell?
No, you're not locked up.
You sleep in a cell but, I mean, you do have a key for your room!
It’s really really good fun Hmm, I'll have to take your word on that one I think Kelly.
Well, let's move swiftly on to maybe a more serious topic.
It certainly seems that more people are travelling, but what are the effects on the countries they visit?
What about the local people?
I mean, are there any negative effects from tourism?
Well, yes. Of course there are always negative effects.
Some studies show that increased tourism brings increased crime local people carrying out crimes against tourists.
What kind of crimes?
Serious or? Oh, Things like stealing cameras or iPhones from tourists is very common.
And they’re relatively easy to steal but I think it’s important to emphasize that millions of tourists travel safely every year!
Yes. I tend to agree.
There are some very positive effects of tourism as well Such as?
Well, of course, tourism brings in money.
Yes. If we think about the number of people who are travelling, lots more money is going to countries and it comes from tourists But what are the effects of money?
Well, we can see the effects of money in countries which can start to develop their infrastructure.
And it’s through Sorry, what do you mean by developing an infrastructure in this context?
Well, like building good roads and hospitals.
Everyone benefits. Right.
Building good roads and hospitals is obviously important but.
Yes, and, another positive effect of tourism is that countries maintain their traditions.
Some countries have kept up some of their customs because it brings in the tourists.
Yeah, I think this can be true.
I mean like in Thailand before international tourism some of the traditional dances.
Like the Nora Dance The what The Nora Dance the name doesn’t really matter.
It's a traditional dance and it had almost totally disappeared by the 1980s.

But it’s spectacular that hotel started putting it on for all the tourists and now there are Nora Dance festivals and competitions all over Thailand Right well, that's a positive way to end the programme.
I'd like to say a big thank you to our guests Kelly and Adrian this week and we'll see you all next week.
Bye. That is the end 15 minutes to complete the written tasks in either Part B1 or Part B2.
